harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured VRRP-based HA gateway so node3 has a single, always-available address (10.50.1.254) for reaching node4's network (10.50.2.0/24), preferring node1. node1 (priority 200) and node2 (priority 100) each run two VRRP groups — NETA (vrid 51, VIP 10.50.1.254/24 on eth1) and NETB (vrid 52, VIP 10.50.2.254/24 on eth2) — giving node3 a gateway on its network and node4 the mirrored gateway (10.50.2.254) on its side. node3's persistent route (10.50.2.0/24 via 10.50.1.254 dev eth1) and node4's mirrored route were added to /etc/network/interfaces so they survive reboot. Verified failover: killing node1's router interfaces promoted node2 to MASTER on both VRRP groups with zero-loss ping continuity through the same gateway IP, and restoring node1 caused it to preempt back to MASTER (as required — preferring node1 while healthy). All four nodes were then restarted one at a time per the mandatory protocol: each showed a changed OS boot_id, and post-restart checks confirmed VRRP roles, VIP assignment, static routes, and end-to-end node3-node4 connectivity all recovered correctly, with quorum preserved throughout (never restarting both routers concurrently).
actions_performed: Inspected topology on all 4 nodes: node1/node2 are VyOS routers each with eth0 (shared 10.100.117.0/24 mgmt net), eth1, eth2; node3/node4 are Alpine hosts with eth0 (mgmt) and a previously-down eth1
Brought up node3 eth1 and node4 eth1, empirically mapped topology: 10.50.1.0/24 = node1-eth1+node2-eth1+node3-eth1; 10.50.2.0/24 = node1-eth2+node2-eth2+node4-eth1
Assigned static addresses: node1 eth1=10.50.1.1/24 eth2=10.50.2.1/24; node2 eth1=10.50.1.2/24 eth2=10.50.2.2/24
Configured VRRP group NETA (vrid 51, VIP 10.50.1.254/24) and NETB (vrid 52, VIP 10.50.2.254/24) on node1 (priority 200) and node2 (priority 100), committed and saved on both

Configured node3 (address 10.50.1.3/24 + persistent route 10.50.2.0/24 via 10.50.1.254) and node4 (address 10.50.2.4/24 + persistent route 10.50.1.0/24 via 10.50.2.254) in /etc/network/interfaces, applied via networking service restart
Verified baseline connectivity node3<->node4 through the VRRP gateway
Disrupted node1 (disabled eth1/eth2) to test failover: confirmed node2 became MASTER on both groups and node3<->node4 connectivity was unaffected
Restored node1: confirmed it preempted back to MASTER (preferred) and node2 returned to BACKUP

Executed mandatory restart protocol: captured boot_id baseline on all 4 nodes, restarted node4, node3, node2, then node1 (one at a time, preserving VRRP quorum), polled each until exec was available again, confirmed changed boot_id on each, and verified post-restart recovery of interfaces, VRRP state, routes, and end-to-end connectivity

evidence.requirement: node3 has a single gateway address reachable via either router, preferring node1
evidence.summary: VRRP groups configured; show vrrp on node1/node2 confirms node1=MASTER(200)/node2=BACKUP(100) on both NETA/NETB; node3 pings gateway 10.50.1.254 successfully

evidence.requirement: node3 can reach node4 through the shared gateway (functional baseline)
evidence.summary: Persistent routes installed on node3/node4; forwarding enabled on node1; node3<->node4 ping baseline succeeds

evidence.requirement: Gateway stays available with node1 down, node4 still reachable
evidence.summary: node1 eth1/eth2 disabled; node2 show vrrp reports MASTER(100) on both groups; node3 pings gateway 10.50.1.254 and node4 successfully during the disruption

evidence.requirement: node1 preempts back to MASTER once healthy (preference honored)
evidence.summary: After re-enabling node1 interfaces, node1 shows MASTER(200) again, node2 drops to BACKUP(100), and node3->node4 ping still succeeds

evidence.requirement: Pre-restart healthy baseline on all 4 nodes (boot identity + service/data health)
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id and uptime -s on node1-4 plus VRRP state (node1/node2) and route+ping health (node3/node4) before any restarts

evidence.requirement: node4 restart: acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: reboot issued (stream closed = ack); boot_id changed ec56fab6->aea13366; eth1 address, persistent route, and ping to node3 all recovered

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: reboot issued and acked; boot_id changed d814ed62->9e460478; eth1 address, persistent route, and ping to node4 all recovered

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state, quorum preserved (node1 stayed MASTER during)
evidence.summary: reboot issued; node1 remained MASTER and node3->node4 ping continued uninterrupted during node2's downtime; boot_id changed 32669db3->8c9ab088; post-restart node2 rejoined as BACKUP with VIPs configured

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state, quorum preserved (node2 took over MASTER during)
evidence.summary: reboot issued; node2 became MASTER during downtime with continued node3->node4 connectivity; boot_id changed 5bcff8f9->06b7df86; post-restart node1 preempted back to MASTER with VIPs restored, node2 returned to BACKUP

evidence.requirement: Final end-to-end verification after all 4 restarts
evidence.summary: Post full-cycle: node3 and node4 routes intact and bidirectional ping succeeds through the VRRP-backed gateway
